h: Shabbos Brings Satisfaction Within Torah’s Endless Ascent

p: to be satisfied with words of Torah,
"One who loves money will not be satisfied with money,"
"One who loves Torah will not be satisfied with Torah";
and at the end of Berachos it is stated (Berachos 64a):
לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
neither in this world nor in the World to Come,
And the Maharsha, of blessed memory, asked:
why, the life of the World to Come
"for the day that is entirely Shabbos
And in truth in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 31a)
But in the Mishnah at the end of Tamid
in the name of Rabbeinu Ovadiah of Bartenura,
he reads "for the One Who lives forever";
But in truth, for Hashem Yisbarach,
when the evil inclination is nullified,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good";
that He rejoiced in His world;
the evil inclination, and death, and suffering.
שֶׁיְּהֵא מַעֲלֶה חֵן לְפָנַי תָּמִיד כֵּן
it would find favor before Me always so."
when the evil inclination will be wholly nullified,
when He slaughters it (as written in Sukkah 52a),
then Hashem Yisbarach will have repose;
and this is "for the day that is entirely Shabbos
and rest for the One Who lives forever."
and from beis midrash to beis midrash.
But from the end of the pasuk,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, כג)
"And it shall be, from new moon to new moon
And "strength" (chayil) means a gathering of Sages,
and this is on each and every Shabbos.
And this is "they go from strength to strength":
that is, on each and every Shabbos
they go from level to level,
when the evil inclination and the bad are nullified.
the more one attains of words of Torah,
כִּי אֲרוּכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר (אִיּוֹב יא, ט)
for "it is longer than the earth," etc. (Iyov 11:9);
and there is no satisfaction in words of Torah
except through the mitzvah of Shabbos,
which is a semblance of the future,
"for the day that is entirely Shabbos and rest";
and they expounded in the holy Zohar:
above the letters of the holy Name,
in the tip of the yud.
And the matter of delight is completeness,
for rest is repose and satisfaction,
"and rest for the One Who lives forever."
